When locking the screen cycles through three options: disconnect, mute only, or do nothing and stay connected. The choice is saved. Mute only keeps the connection and silences remote speech until you unlock. If you had already muted it manually, it stays muted. You can use other apps while connected. Use Disconnect to end the session.

In NVDA, choose Allow this computer to be controlled and use the same server and key. Connect and open Remote keyboard.

Three fingers down switch between Keyboard and Control modes. Three fingers up open the menu. Back returns to the form. Gestures can be reassigned; Back always provides an exit.

In Control mode, dot 6 prepares Control, 5 Alt, 3 Shift and 2 NVDA. Modifiers can be combined; tap again to cancel one. They are consumed by the next key. Enter a braille letter to send its key: dot 6 then c sends Ctrl+C; dot 2 then t sends NVDA+T.

Hold dot 1 and swipe from dot 4 to send the corresponding arrow. Without holding 1, swipe from 4 right for Tab, left for Shift+Tab, up for Page up and down for Page down. Two fingers right send Enter; left sends Escape.

In Keyboard mode, dots go to the braille input table configured in NVDA. One finger right enters space; left erases a cell or character. Two fingers right commit braille and press Enter. Two fingers up commit without space. Letters, symbols, numbers and contracted braille depend on the NVDA table, which may differ from the CAN Talk table.

Reassign remote gestures lets you choose a mode, capture a gesture without sending it to the PC and assign an action or shortcut. Assignments are saved separately for each mode. Restore defaults for one mode as needed. Learning announces actions without executing them on the PC.

Layout, orientation and calibration use the CAN Talk braille surface. Hold all dots to calibrate. Menus use normal touch exploration. The surface requires Android 11 or later. You can leave this screen and stay connected. Use Disconnect to end the session.
Three fingers down: switch mode. Three fingers up: menu. Back: return to the form.
Perform the gesture to assign in %1$s. It will not be sent to the PC. Back cancels capture.
Restore default gestures for %1$s? The other mode will keep its assignments.
Send a key or custom shortcut
Learning enabled. Gestures announce their action without sending it to the PC. Use the menu to leave learning.
Learning disabled. Commands will be sent to the PC again.
Prepared: %1$s. Applies to the next key.

Physical modifiers in Control mode: hold dot 5 until the vibration, then swipe from dot 4 right to cycle through windows or left to go back. Keep dot 5 down between swipes. Release dot 5 to select the window. While holding 5, swipe two other fingers left for Escape to cancel; lift the held point before starting again.

Hold dot 3 with dot 1 and swipe from dot 4 to select with Shift+arrows. Hold dot 6 with dot 1 for Control+arrows to move by words. Holding dot 2 provides the NVDA modifier. Up to three held fingers can be combined. A modifier tap still prepares it for one key.

Held modifiers follow the assigned dot action. Capture a hold to assign or disable it separately. Learning describes the combination without sending keys to the PC. Opening a menu, switching modes, exiting or losing focus releases held keys. If the connection breaks, releases may not reach the PC.
